name: Pedaiah
overview: Pedaiah was a male member of the tribe of Manasseh, noted primarily for being the father of Joel. His mention is brief and focused on his paternal role within the genealogical records of Israel. There are no additional notes or distinguishing events recorded about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Pedaiah means "y-h-v-h ransoms," reflecting a theologically significant meaning that God redeems or rescues. This proper name, though not indicated as given directly by God, carries the weight of divine deliverance inherent in its Hebrew roots.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly identifies Pedaiah as a descendant of Manasseh and as the father of Joel. Beyond these relationships, no further family connections are recorded in the biblical text concerning Pedaiah.
scriptureSignificance: Pedaiah's significance lies in his role within the genealogical lineage of the tribe of Manasseh, serving as the father of Joel. This connection situates him within the broader history of Israel's tribal organization and leadership. His inclusion in the biblical record, though brief, contributes to the preservation of God's covenantal people through their family lines.
